$comment: v2.7 33 W3 N6 fixture: 20 windows of 6 replies (oldest first, the last is the latest reply), English, authored, labelled before the miner was run. 10 loops, 10 fresh. A loops window repeats a phrase, an opener or a stock construction in its latest reply that also appears in at least two earlier replies; a fresh window does not, though fresh traps repeat names, places and a quoted player line. hot lists the phrases a reader would name.

rows.label: loops
hot: a shiver ran down her spine
replies: Mara pushes the door open. A shiver ran down her spine as the cold air of the crypt met her face.
The torches gutter. Somewhere below, water drips in a slow, patient rhythm.
Mara kneels by the sarcophagus and traces the carved name. A shiver ran down her spine at the touch of the stone.
Brother Ivo hums a hymn under his breath, too loud for the quiet.
The lid shifts a finger's width. A shiver ran down her spine and she pulls her hand back.
Dust sighs out of the gap. Mara steadies herself, and a shiver ran down her spine as something inside rattles.

rows.label: loops
replies: Pip grins, eyes glinting with mischief, and tosses you the stolen apple.
The market is loud with gulls and hawkers selling eels by the pound.
"You owe me one," Pip says, eyes glinting with mischief as the guard turns the corner.
A cart rumbles past, scattering pigeons across the square.
Pip leans on the fountain, eyes glinting with mischief, counting coins that are not hers.
She winks at you, eyes glinting with mischief, and vanishes into the crowd before the baker can shout.

rows.label: loops
replies: The wind howls through the pass as the column halts at the ridge.
Captain Orrel studies the map, tapping a gloved finger on the river ford.
The wind howls through the tents, tugging at every rope in the camp.
A scout rides in, breathless, with news of riders to the east.
The wind howls through the gorge while the horses stamp and blow.
The wind howls through the broken watchtower as you climb the last stair.

rows.label: loops
replies: Lysa looks at the letter for a long time. Her face shows not anger, but something softer.
The rain has stopped. Water still runs off the eaves in thin silver threads.
When you mention her brother, she pauses. There is not anger, but something softer, in the way she sets down her cup.
The innkeeper brings bread and a bowl of thin soup.
Lysa folds the letter into quarters. Not anger, but something softer, crosses her face.
She meets your eyes, and what you see there is not anger, but something softer, almost like relief.

rows.label: loops
hot: a mix of fear and determination
replies: Tomas grips the rope, a mix of fear and determination on his young face.
The cliff falls away into white spray far below.
He looks up at you, a mix of fear and determination in his voice as he asks how far.
Gulls wheel overhead, shrieking at the intruders on their ledge.
Tomas steps onto the ledge with a mix of fear and determination.
With a mix of fear and determination, Tomas lets go of the rope and reaches for the next hold.

rows.label: loops
hot: she didn't know she was holding
replies: Elin lets out a breath she didn't know she was holding when the guard walks past.
The archive smells of mould and old wax. Shelves vanish into the dark.
When the lock clicks open, Elin releases a breath she didn't know she was holding.
A rat scurries between the stacks and is gone.
She finds the ledger. Elin exhales a breath she didn't know she was holding and opens it to the last page.
The page is blank. Elin lets out a breath she didn't know she was holding, then laughs at herself.

rows.label: loops
hot: a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips
replies: Kael folds his arms, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.
The duelling yard is empty but for the two of you and a rack of blunted blades.
"Again?" Kael asks, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.
Sparrows bicker on the wall above the yard.
He tosses you a practice sword, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips as you fumble the catch.
Kael circles you slowly, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips, and waits for your first move.

rows.label: loops
hot: somewhere in the distance, a dog barks
replies: The village sleeps. Somewhere in the distance, a dog barks.
You knock twice on the miller's door. No light shows behind the shutters.
Footsteps cross the yard and stop. Somewhere in the distance, a dog barks.
The door opens a crack and a lantern swings into your face.
The miller shakes his head and shuts the door. Somewhere in the distance, a dog barks.
You stand alone in the lane again. Somewhere in the distance, a dog barks, then falls silent.

rows.label: loops
hot: the weight of his words hangs in the air
replies: The old king falls silent. The weight of his words hangs in the air.
Courtiers shuffle their feet and avoid each other's eyes.
"Then it is war," says the marshal. The weight of his words hangs in the air.
A servant drops a goblet; nobody turns to look.
The prince says nothing at first. When he speaks, the weight of his words hangs in the air.
"I will ride at dawn," the prince says, and the weight of his words hangs in the air long after.

rows.label: loops
replies: Dax flashes a crooked grin and slides the cards across the table.
The smoke in the gambling den is thick enough to chew.
Dax flashes a crooked grin when the dealer turns the last card.
A drunk at the next table starts a song nobody else knows.
Dax flashes a crooked grin at the bouncer, who does not grin back.
Dax flashes a crooked grin, pockets the winnings and nods toward the back door.

rows.label: fresh
replies: Mara and Brother Ivo reach the Silver Stag just before the gates close.
The common room of the Silver Stag is half empty; a fire burns low in the hearth.
Brother Ivo orders two bowls of stew and asks the landlord about the road north.
The landlord of the Silver Stag says the bridge washed out three days ago.
Mara spreads the map on the table and marks the ford upstream.
Brother Ivo yawns, and Mara sends him to bed while she studies the route to the Silver Stag's sister inn at Harrow.

rows.label: fresh
replies: "I will find the bell," you said, and Sela nods as if she has heard it before.
She leads you down to the harbour where the fishing boats are drawn up on the shingle.
An old net-mender points at the drowned tower beyond the breakwater.
Sela borrows a skiff and rows while you watch the water for rocks.
The tower's door is under a foot of water. Sela ties the boat to a rusted ring.
Inside, weed hangs from the beams, and far above a bronze shape catches the light.

rows.label: fresh
replies: The morning is grey and the road is wet from the night's rain.
By noon the clouds break and a farmer offers you a ride on his cart.
His daughter asks where you are going and laughs at the answer.
The cart leaves you at a crossroads marked by a leaning stone.
You choose the left road, which climbs through birch woods toward the hills.
At dusk you see smoke rising from a hut at the edge of a frozen lake.

rows.label: fresh
replies: The bandit lunges; you turn the blade aside and feel the jolt up your arm.
A second one circles behind the overturned wagon, looking for an opening.
Ruk throws a pot of lamp oil, and the wagon catches with a dull roar.
The first bandit drops his sword and runs for the trees.
The other surrenders, kneeling in the mud with his hands on his head.
Ruk binds his wrists with harness leather and asks who sent them.

rows.label: fresh
replies: "You came back," Hesper says, without looking up from her loom.
"The guild will not wait forever. They want an answer by the new moon."
She cuts the thread and holds the cloth up to the window.
"My mother wove this pattern for the old duke. Nobody remembers it now."
"Tell them I accept, but only if the apprentices are paid."
Hesper folds the cloth and presses it into your arms for the guild master.

rows.label: fresh
replies: He nods.
The candle flickers out.
Silence.
A knock at the door.
Nobody answers it.
The knocking stops and footsteps walk away down the hall.

rows.label: fresh
replies: In the Hall of Echoes the choir rehearses a dirge for the dead queen.
You slip past the choir and into the Hall of Echoes' vestry.
The vestry holds robes, candles and a locked chest bound in iron.
Brother Anselm catches you at the chest and demands to know your business.
You claim the dean sent you for fresh candles; he does not believe you.
He calls for the wardens, and their boots ring on the stone of the Hall of Echoes.

rows.label: fresh
replies: Ilse sharpens her knife on a whetstone and says nothing about last night.
Bram counts the arrows twice and frowns at the total.
Ilse finally asks whether you saw the lights over the marsh.
Bram says the lights are marsh gas, and that only fools follow them.
Ilse says her grandmother followed them once and came back with silver.
Bram tells her to pack for the marsh, grumbling the whole time.

rows.label: fresh
replies: The ferryman spits into the river and holds out his hand for the fare.
Halfway across, a fog comes down and swallows both banks.
The ferryman spits into the river again and mutters about bad luck.
Something bumps the hull from below, gently, like a curious dog.
The fog lifts as suddenly as it came, and the far bank is close.
You step onto the jetty while the ferryman pushes off without a word.

rows.label: fresh
replies: The quartermaster lists what is left: twelve sacks of flour, four barrels of salt pork.
He adds two crates of arrows and a cask of lamp oil to the tally.
The cook complains that the flour is damp and half of it is weevils.
Captain Orrel orders the salt pork rationed to one strip a day.
A soldier asks whether the lamp oil could be used to fire the enemy's palisade.
The captain likes the idea and sends for the engineer.
